messages.author: 5f533b50135a7f86
messages.subject: R packages for DAGs
parts:
Hey D-RUG, 

I need to draw and analyze a rather complicated directed acyclic graph for one of my projects.  I’ve found a few R packages for drawing DAGs, such as dagR and daggitty, but they haven’t been updated in a few years.  Does anyone happen to know what the cool kids are using to draw DAGs in 2019?  

Thanks, 
Dan
----

Postdoctoral Researcher
Data Science Initiative
University of California, Davis

messages.author: e0691e26c9cf72eb
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: R packages for DAGs
parts:
Since DAGs is a subset/type of graph network, how about igraph?
https://rdrr.io/cran/igraph/man/is_dag.html implies that igraph knows
about this type of network.

And if you want to fancy up the plotting
https://rich-iannone.github.io/DiagrammeR/#features

Enjoy,
Alex Mandel, PhD

Center for Spatial Sciences
https://spatial.ucdavis.edu
Geospatial and Farming Systems Research Consortium
https://gfc.ucdavis.edu

messages.author: 24ea9f27d1bb7ea1
messages.subject: R packages for DAGs
parts: I highly recommend tidygraph for graph analysis and ggraph for visualization. tidygraph operates on top of igraph so you can still use all the functionality it provides.

messages.author: d0c629ef4df1de7c
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: R packages for DAGs
parts:
The cool kids have been using graphviz since the 90's. It still rocks for producing publication quality pdf's. I've been exporting graphs from R's 'igraph' package to dot (graphviz) format, and then sometimes I tweak that a bit before producing a pdf with the 'dot' command. For example: https://github.com/clarkfitzg/makeParallel/blob/master/R/plot.R#L132

Best,
Clark
